decision: Retain current swizzled-shared -> 128-bit vector FC2 writeback. Direct-register candidate is slower; production source restored, patch and measurements archived.
notes: Only nominal 8192/20480 tested, with 10% token-count variation and new random routes/gates every call.
Both variants already use 128-bit global stores. This experiment removes FC2 shared staging and its ready barrier, but keeps the completion join and terminal rank publication.
Shared capacity intentionally unchanged to isolate writeback, with the same 226304 dynamic shared bytes and 168 reported registers.

For N256, staged writeback assigns 32 lanes to one row (512B); quad-shuffle direct writeback assigns four lanes to each of eight rows (64B per row per instruction). These layout and shuffle differences are plausible causes, not a separately profiled causal decomposition.
Cached mode is forward-only with Saved X/GU; no backward timing or new backward validation in this ablation.
